chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me who said: Abu Sa'id al-Adamy narrated to me who said: Al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Abu Umar al-Ajami who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'O Abu Umar! Indeed, nine-tenths of religion is in the concealing of faith (Taqiyyah), and there is no religion for one who has no Taqiyyah. And Taqiyyah is in everything except in drinking Nabidh and wiping over the foot-wear (Khuffayn).'

key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Concealing of faith or state to avoid harm
key_terms.النَّبِيذ: Fermented drink made from dates or grapes

ai.seo_question: What are the exceptions to the rule of Taqiyyah in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates Taqiyyah not merely as a defensive tactic but as the fundamental essence of religious practice, comprising nine-tenths of the faith, particularly in the context of Shia historical experiences under Umayyad and Abbasid rule. While generally applicable to all acts of worship and transactions, the hadith specifies two exceptions—drinking Nabidh and wiping over the Khuff—indicating that these specific rulings must be performed openly regardless of the need for concealment. This distinction highlights the balance between strategic discretion and the public affirmation of specific legal obligations within Shia jurisprudence.
